facts.claim: The power dissipated by a resistor is P = IV = I^2 R = V^2/R (Joule heating).
facts.quote: With a resistor, the voltage drop across the resistor is dissipated as heat. [...] The power dissipated by a resistor has the form [Equation 9.13, MathML: P = I²R = V²/R]
facts.document_title: 9.5 Electrical Energy and Power - University Physics Volume 2 | OpenStax
facts.location: Section 9.5, subsections 'Power in Electric Circuits' and 'Electric Power', Equation 9.13
facts.applies_to: Ohmic resistor (any heater, wiring or resistive element) carrying current I with resistance R

facts.claim: Every cryocooler has a load curve/capacity map relating the maximum heat load it can remove to its operating temperature; loads above the nominal operating point drive the stage to a higher temperature, and the base temperature is set by the balance between cooling capacity and parasitic load.
facts.quote: For all cryocoolers there is a relation between the maximum heat load that they can dissipate and their operating temperature, known as a load curve, or in a two-parameter space, a capacity map.
facts.document_title: Design and characterization of the POLARBEAR-2b and POLARBEAR-2c cosmic microwave background cryogenic receivers
facts.location: Section 2.1 '50 K and 4 K Refrigeration', p. 3-4 (arXiv v1)
facts.applies_to: Cryocoolers in general; measured on a Cryomech PT415 pulse tube in the PB-2b receiver

facts.claim: Heat loads above (below) a cryocooler's operating point give higher (lower) stage temperatures; the base temperature is a balance of cooling capacity and parasitic loading (steady-state heat balance).
facts.quote: Heat loads above (below) these operating points results in higher (lower) system temperatures [...] The lowest temperature reached by each stage of the PTC is referred to as the base temperature, which is a balance of the PTC cooling capacity and the parasitic loading.
facts.document_title: Design and characterization of the POLARBEAR-2b and POLARBEAR-2c cosmic microwave background cryogenic receivers
facts.location: Section 2.1 '50 K and 4 K Refrigeration'; see also Figure 4 (load curve of PT415 second stage, base 2.54 K at 0 W)
facts.applies_to: Pulse tube cryocooler (PT415) stages; general steady-state cryostat heat balance

facts.claim: The f-number is the focal length divided by the aperture diameter, f/# = f/D, approximately 1/(2 NA) for small acceptance angles.
facts.quote: the f -number is given by the ratio of the focal length f of the lens and the diameter D of the aperture controlling the light into the lens (see Figure 26.17 (b)). If the acceptance angle is small the NA of the lens can also be used as given below. [Equation 26.24: f/# = f/D ≈ 1/(2NA)]

facts.claim: Edmund Optics defines f/# as focal length divided by effective aperture diameter, defines NA as the sine of the marginal-ray angle in image space, and gives NA = 1/(2 x f/#).
facts.quote: Fundamentally, f/# is the ratio of the focal length, (f), of the lens to the effective aperture diameter (Ø_EA) [...] The NA of a lens is defined as the sine of the angle made by the marginal ray and optical axis in image space [...] It is important to remember that f/# and NA are inversely related. [Equation 3: NA = 1/(2 × (f/#))]
facts.document_title: System Throughput, f/#, and Numerical Aperture | Edmund Optics
facts.location: Equation 1 (f/# = f/Ø_EA), section 'f/# and Numerical Aperture', Equation 3 and Table 3
facts.applies_to: Imaging lenses at infinite working distance (in air, n = 1); Table 3 pairs e.g. f/2 with NA 0.25

facts.claim: Image-side NA relates to lens geometry as NA = n sin[arctan(D/2f)] ≈ nD/(2f) (thin-lens tan(theta) = D/2f, i.e. N = 1/(2 tan theta)); for well-corrected lenses N is almost exactly 1/(2NA) even at large NA.
facts.quote: The approximation holds when the numerical aperture is small, but it turns out that for well-corrected optical systems such as camera lenses, a more detailed analysis shows that N is almost exactly equal to 1/(2NA i ) even at large numerical apertures.
facts.document_title: Numerical aperture - Wikipedia
facts.location: Section 'Numerical aperture versus f-number' (formula NA_i = n sin θ = n sin[arctan(D/2f)] ≈ n D/2f, and following paragraph)
facts.applies_to: Image-side NA of a lens focused at infinity; tertiary source (Wikipedia, citing Kingslake 1951)

notes: 1) Equations on OpenStax and Edmund pages are rendered as MathML/LaTeX; text in square brackets inside quotes is an editorial transcription of the equation and '[...]' marks omitted text, everything else is verbatim. 2) The QD 1307-010 brochure (Rev. G0, as fetched) does NOT state charge rates in Oe/s, contrary to the task brief; only 'Min Time to Full Field'. Charge rates were taken from QD catalogue 1084-500 (Rev. D0 hosted by UNT; Rev. A2 hosted by KTH), third-party hosted copies of a QD document. In the pdftotext layout the value line appears one row above its label; PyMuPDF line coordinates confirm label and value share y=155 on PDF page 3. Consistency check: 9 T = 90 kOe / 200 Oe/s = 450 s < 480 s; 12 T: 120 kOe/100 Oe/s = 1200 s < 1500 s; 14 T: 140 kOe/100 Oe/s = 1400 s < 2400 s, so the quoted times-to-full-field are consistent with t = dB/rate. Oe to T conversion uses B = mu0*H (1 Oe <-> 1e-4 T in vacuum). Rev A2 lists EverCool II (not DynaCool) 14 T at 160 Oe/s; rev D0 lists it at 100 Oe/s. 3) Heat balance: no single manufacturer manual sentence 'load must be <= cooling power' was found; the POLARBEAR-2 paper's load-curve statements (pm_002/003) are the closest verbatim justification. Capacity rising with T: pm_005/006 (same cooler, 80 mW at 3 K vs 240 mW at 4.2 K) and pm_008/009 (Bluefors 14 uW at 20 mK vs 450 uW at 100 mK). PT415 rating (pm_004) is a secondary citation in a paper. 4) N = 1/(2 tan theta) appears only implicitly via the Wikipedia thin-lens formula NA = n sin[arctan(D/2f)]; Wikipedia also notes that for coma/spherical-corrected lenses N ~ 1/(2NA) is nearly exact, so the tan form is the thin-lens approximation. 5) Linkam: no L/h consumption or hold-time hours found; only '2L dewar' and 'a day of cooling experiments' (LNP95 PDF hosted by McCrone). The Linkam THMS600/T95 manual at mmk.su.se could not be fetched (TLS certificate mismatch) and was not bypassed. LNP96-specific dewar data not found. 6) arXiv DOIs (10.48550/...) and 10.1021/acsomega.2c03083 were verified by HTTP 302 from doi.org; the arXiv abs pages list no journal DOI.
